title: Why Earth Has Seasons, and It Isn't Distance
description: Why the tilt of Earth's axis, not its distance from the Sun, brings summer and winter, from NASA and NOAA.
narration: Does summer arrive because Earth swings closer to the Sun? Many people believe summer comes when Earth is closest to the Sun. But that idea is incorrect. In the Northern Hemisphere, winter arrives while Earth is nearest the Sun, and summer arrives when it is farthest. The real reason is that Earth's axis is tilted instead of standing straight up. As Earth travels around the Sun, the axis keeps pointing the same direction. So sometimes the northern half leans toward the Sun, and sometimes the southern half does. The half tilted toward the Sun gets its rays more directly, and that half has summer. Because the two poles are at opposite ends of Earth, the seasons are opposite too.
